frontMatter.value: Concentrate validation, parsing and error handling at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs), trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions; and let no failure become success-shaped output: no catch block returning a default, no fabricated data, a test that forces each changed integration to fail. Use when validating input or handling an error at a boundary, when writing a catch block, a default value, a retry or a fallback, when a dependency fails during the work, and when a deadline or a demonstration makes a working-looking result tempting.

passages.reason: The habit's title is its roster name, boundaries, which R22 gives the habit boundary-discipline and fail-loud became.
passages.gist: The title is boundaries, which boundary-discipline and fail-loud became

passages.text: boundaries is the habit for the moment input is validated or an error handled where data enters the system, a catch block, a default, a retry or a fallback is written, a dependency fails during the work, or a deadline or a demonstration makes a working-looking result tempting, at whatever step the work is in, most often build. It writes no record of its own: the negative-path tests it asks for are named in the step's section and the reply. A system boundary here is where outside data enters, a CLI, a config file, the network, an external API; between two modules of one program, deep-modules' word is seam.
passages.reason: One opening paragraph in the habit's own voice: the situations the block's rows key it by, that it writes no record of its own and where its tests are named, and which boundary it means, since deep-modules says seam for the place between modules.
passages.gist: Opens the habit: when it applies; boundaries are where outside data enters
